_comment: Short answers to common questions children ask about the world, used by the rule-based response engine (services/response_engine.py) when a question matches no rule. Each pattern is a case-insensitive regular expression matched against the child's question; the first match wins, so put specific patterns before general ones. Keep answers short, simple and well established.

answers.pattern: \bwhy do butterflies have wings\b|\bhow do butterflies fly\b
answers.answer: Butterflies use their wings to fly from flower to flower to drink nectar. Their bright colors can also warn birds to stay away!
A shot might pinch for a second, but it's over really fast! Taking a deep breath or squeezing a grown-up's hand can help.

answers.pattern: \bhow do robots work\b|\bhow does a robot work\b
answers.answer: Robots have a computer 'brain' that follows instructions called a program, sensors to notice what's around them, and motors to move!

answers.pattern: \bwhere does snow come from\b|\bhow is snow made\b
answers.answer: Snow forms high up in very cold clouds. Tiny water drops freeze into ice crystals, and the crystals stick together into snowflakes!
Lightning is super bright and thunder is really loud, and lightning can be dangerous, so it's smart to stay inside during a storm. Feeling scared of it is totally normal!

answers.pattern: \b(can|do) (fish|dogs|cats|pets|animals|hamsters) go to heaven\b|\bwhere do (pets|animals) go when they die\b
answers.answer: That's a really big question. Different families believe different things, so it's a good one to ask your mom or dad about. It sounds like you loved your pet a lot.
Most seeds sprout in about 1 to 2 weeks. Tomato plants usually have tomatoes about 2 to 3 months after planting. Keep watering them!

answers.pattern: \b(will|does|is) the tooth fairy (come|real|coming)\b|\bis the tooth fairy real\b
answers.answer: Lots of kids put their tooth under their pillow and hope for a visit! That's a fun one to ask your mom or dad about.

answers.pattern: \bhow much (money )?(do you get|does the tooth fairy (give|leave|bring))\b
answers.answer: It's different for every family! Some kids find a coin, and some find a dollar. Your mom or dad would know best!
Start with a strong base of stone blocks, build tall walls with a tower at each corner, and add a gate! You could look up castle ideas with a grown-up too.
Pick a spot, build four walls with wood planks, add a roof, a door and some windows, and put a bed inside so you can sleep through the night!
Lots of cats like the taste of milk, but most grown-up cats can't digest it well, so it can upset their tummies. Water is best for them!

answers.pattern: \bcan dogs (eat|have) chocolate\b|\bis chocolate bad for dogs\b
answers.answer: No! Chocolate can make dogs really sick. If a dog eats chocolate, tell a grown-up right away.
Dogs wag their tails to show how they feel. A loose, happy wag usually means they're excited or friendly!
Cats sleep 12 to 16 hours a day! They save their energy for short bursts of running, pouncing and playing.
Yes, in their own way! Fish rest by slowing down and staying still, but most can't close their eyes because they don't have eyelids.
Hamsters usually live about 2 to 3 years, and guinea pigs about 5 to 7 years.
Most dogs live about 10 to 13 years. Smaller dogs often live longer than big dogs!
Indoor cats often live about 12 to 18 years, and some live even longer!
Nope! A shark's skeleton is made of cartilage, the same bendy stuff that's in your nose and ears.
A knight moves in an L shape: two squares one way, then one square to the side. It's the only piece that can jump over other pieces!
A bishop moves diagonally, as many squares as it wants, so it always stays on the same color!
A rook moves in straight lines, up, down, or sideways, as many squares as it wants!
The queen is the most powerful piece! She can move any number of squares in a straight line or diagonally.
The king moves just one square in any direction. Keep him safe, because if he's trapped, it's checkmate!
A pawn moves forward one square, or two on its very first move. It captures diagonally, one square forward!
Checkmate is when the king is under attack and has no way to escape. That's how you win a chess game!
Check means the king is under attack and must get safe right away. Stalemate is when a player has no legal move but isn't in check, and the game is a tie!
Castling is a special move where the king moves two squares toward a rook, and the rook jumps to the other side of the king. It helps keep your king safe!
A good start is to move your center pawns, bring out your knights and bishops, and castle to keep your king safe. Lots of players like the Italian Game!

answers.pattern: \bhow (do|does) (you|i|a person) win (at |in |a )?chess\b|\bhow do you play chess\b
answers.answer: In chess, you win by checkmating the other player's king, which means trapping it so it can't escape. Each piece moves in its own special way!
A fraction is a part of something whole! If you cut a pizza into 4 equal slices, one slice is 1/4, or one fourth, of the pizza.
A decimal is another way to write part of a number, like 0.5, which means one half!
A prime number can only be divided evenly by 1 and itself, like 2, 3, 5, 7, and 11!
Even numbers can be split into two equal groups, like 2, 4, and 6. Odd numbers have one left over, like 1, 3, and 5!
Computers follow lists of instructions called programs, super fast! They use electricity and tiny switches to do math, remember things, and show pictures.
T. rex was a meat-eater! It probably hunted other dinosaurs, like Triceratops.
Sunflowers can grow taller than a grown-up! Most get about 5 to 10 feet tall, and some grow even taller.
Hamsters eat special hamster food, seeds, and little bits of veggies like carrots. Ask a grown-up which foods are safe!
Rabbits mostly eat hay, plus some leafy greens and a little bit of special rabbit food!
Dogs eat dog food made just for them. Some people food, like chocolate and grapes, can make dogs sick!
Cats eat cat food made just for them. They need meat to stay healthy!
Pet fish eat fish flakes or pellets. Just a tiny pinch is enough!
Many turtles eat a mix of plants, bugs, and special turtle food!
Lots of birds eat seeds, fruit, and bugs!
Whiskers help cats feel what's around them, even in the dark, and tell them if they can fit through a space!
Whales and dolphins are mammals, not fish! They breathe air, so they come up to the surface to breathe.
Yes! Sharks are fish. Their skeletons are made of cartilage, the same bendy stuff that's in your ears!
Nope! Spiders have 8 legs, so they're arachnids, not insects. Insects have 6 legs.
A tomato is a fruit, because it has seeds inside! But people usually cook with it like a vegetable.
Nope! Bats are mammals, and they're the only mammals that can really fly.
The sky looks blue because sunlight bounces off the air, and blue light bounces around the most!
At sunset, sunlight travels through more air to reach you, so the blue light gets scattered away and the orange and red light is left!

answers.pattern: \bwhy is it dark at night\b|\bwhy does it get dark\b|\bwhere does the sun go\b
answers.answer: The Earth spins like a top! When your side of the Earth turns away from the Sun, it's night for you.

answers.pattern: \bwhy (do|does) (we have|it have|the earth have) seasons\b|\bwhy (are there|do we have) seasons\b
answers.answer: The Earth is tilted! When your part of the Earth leans toward the Sun, it's summer, and when it leans away, it's winter.
The Moon is about 239,000 miles (384,000 km) away. It took astronauts about 3 days to get there!
The Sun is about 93 million miles (150 million km) away. Its light takes about 8 minutes to reach us!
The surface of the Sun is about 10,000°F (5,500°C), and the middle is millions of degrees!
The Sun is so big that about a million Earths could fit inside it!

answers.pattern: \bwhat is the sun\b|\bis the sun a star\b
answers.answer: The Sun is a star! It's a giant ball of hot, glowing gas, and it's the closest star to Earth.
The Moon doesn't really change shape. We just see different amounts of its sunny side as it goes around Earth!

answers.pattern: \bwhy can (we|you|i) see the moon\b.*\bday\b|\bmoon\b.*\bduring the day\b
answers.answer: The Moon is bright enough to see in the day sometimes, because sunlight bounces off it all the time, day or night!
The Moon is made of rock and dust. Astronauts brought some Moon rocks back to Earth!
There are 8 planets in our solar system: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune!
Jupiter is the biggest planet. More than 1,000 Earths could fit inside it!
Mercury is the smallest planet, and it's also the closest one to the Sun.
Venus is the hottest planet, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun. Its thick clouds trap the heat!
Pluto is a dwarf planet! Scientists decided in 2006 that it's too small to be called a regular planet.
Saturn's rings are made of billions of pieces of ice and rock, some as small as sand and some as big as a house!
Mars looks red because its ground has lots of rusty iron dust!
Stars are giant balls of hot, glowing gas, like our Sun, just very, very far away!
Stars twinkle because their light wiggles as it passes through the moving air around Earth!
There are more stars in the universe than anyone can count, maybe more than all the grains of sand on Earth's beaches!
A black hole is a place in space where gravity pulls so hard that not even light can get out!
Gravity is a pull that everything has. The Earth is so big that its pull keeps us on the ground and makes things fall down!

answers.pattern: \bwhy don'?t we fall off the earth\b|\bwhy don'?t people fall off\b
answers.answer: Gravity pulls everything toward the middle of the Earth, so no matter where you stand, down is toward the ground!
The Earth is about 4.5 billion years old! That's really, really old.

answers.pattern: \bis the earth round\b|\bwhy is the earth round\b
answers.answer: Yes! The Earth is shaped like a ball. Gravity pulls everything toward the middle, which makes big things in space round.
In space, astronauts float! They sleep in sleeping bags tied to the wall and eat food from pouches so crumbs don't float away.
Rainbows happen when sunlight shines through raindrops. The drops split the light into all its colors!

answers.pattern: \bwhy (does it|do we get) rain\b|\bwhere does rain come from\b|\bhow does rain\b|\bwhy does it rain\b
answers.answer: Clouds are made of tiny drops of water. When the drops bunch together and get heavy, they fall as rain!

answers.pattern: \bwhat are clouds made of\b|\bwhat is a cloud\b|\bhow do clouds\b
answers.answer: Clouds are made of billions of tiny water drops or ice crystals floating in the air!

answers.pattern: \bhow does snow\b|\bwhy does it snow\b|\bwhat is snow\b
answers.answer: Snow happens when it's so cold up in the clouds that the water freezes into tiny ice crystals, which fall as snowflakes!
Every snowflake has six sides, but they grow in so many ways that two snowflakes almost never look exactly alike!
Thunder is the sound lightning makes. Lightning heats the air so fast that it goes BOOM!
Lightning is a giant spark of electricity that jumps between clouds or between a cloud and the ground!
Light travels much faster than sound, so you see the flash first and hear the thunder after!
Wind is moving air! When the Sun warms some places more than others, the air moves around to even things out.
A tornado is a spinning tube of wind that reaches from a storm cloud down to the ground. If there's a tornado warning, go to a safe room with a grown-up!

answers.pattern: \bwhat is a volcano\b|\bwhy do volcanoes\b|\bhow do volcanoes\b
answers.answer: A volcano is an opening in the Earth where melted rock called magma comes up. When it comes out, it's called lava!
The ground is made of giant pieces called plates that slowly move. When they slip against each other, the ground shakes!
Rivers carry tiny bits of salt from rocks into the ocean, and over millions of years it added up!
Water soaks up red light and leaves the blue, so lots of deep water looks blue!
Most ocean waves are made by wind blowing across the water!
Tides happen because the Moon's gravity pulls on the oceans, making the water rise and fall each day!
The deepest spot in the ocean is about 7 miles (11 km) deep. That's deeper than Mount Everest is tall!
Mount Everest is the tallest mountain above sea level. It's about 29,000 feet (8,849 m) tall!
The Nile in Africa and the Amazon in South America are the two longest rivers. Scientists still argue about which one is longer!
The Pacific Ocean is the biggest ocean. It's bigger than all the land on Earth put together!
Russia is the biggest country by land, and China and India have the most people!
There are 7 continents: Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Australia, Europe, North America, and South America!
There are about 195 countries in the world, and the United States has 50 states!

answers.pattern: \bwhy is the grass green\b|\bwhy are (plants|leaves) green\b
answers.answer: Plants are green because of chlorophyll, a green helper that uses sunlight to make food for the plant!
In the fall, trees stop making the green stuff in their leaves, so the yellow, orange, and red colors show through!
Plants need sunlight, water, and air. They use sunlight to turn water and air into food!

answers.pattern: \bwhy do flowers smell\b|\bwhy do flowers have\b
answers.answer: Flowers use their colors and smells to invite bees and butterflies, which help them make seeds!

answers.pattern: \bhow do bees make honey\b|\bwhat is honey\b
answers.answer: Bees drink sweet nectar from flowers, bring it back to the hive, and turn it into honey!
Some trees live for thousands of years! A bristlecone pine in California is almost 5,000 years old.
Most scientists think a giant asteroid hit Earth about 66 million years ago and changed the weather so much that the dinosaurs died out.
Some of the biggest dinosaurs were long-necked giants like Argentinosaurus, which may have been over 100 feet long!
T. rex was one of the biggest meat-eating dinosaurs. It had huge teeth, but its arms were really short!
Yes! Scientists think birds are living relatives of dinosaurs.
Penguins can't fly because their wings are made for swimming instead! They 'fly' through the water super fast.
Birds flap their wings to push air down, and that lifts them up. Their bones are hollow, so they're really light!
Birds sing to talk to each other, like to say 'this is my spot' or to find a friend!
The blue whale is the biggest animal ever, even bigger than the biggest dinosaurs!
The cheetah is the fastest land animal. It can run about 70 miles per hour! The peregrine falcon is even faster when it dives.
Sloths are some of the slowest animals. They move so slowly that tiny plants can grow on their fur!
Some of the smallest animals are too tiny to see without a microscope! The smallest bird is the bee hummingbird, about the size of a bee.
The giraffe is the tallest animal. It can be taller than a basketball hoop!
Long necks help giraffes reach leaves high up in trees that other animals can't get to!
Cats often purr when they're happy and relaxed, and sometimes to calm themselves down!
Dogs wag their tails and bark to talk! A wagging tail often means they're excited or happy.
Dogs smell the world the way we see it! Their noses are thousands of times better than ours.
Fish breathe with gills, which take oxygen out of the water as it flows through them!
Fish do rest! Most can't close their eyes, but they slow down and stay still to rest.
Scientists think zebra stripes might help keep biting flies away, and maybe help them stay cool!
Some animals hibernate, which means they sleep through the winter when there isn't much food, and wake up in spring!
A caterpillar makes a chrysalis around itself, and inside, its body changes into a butterfly. It's called metamorphosis!
Spiders have 8 legs! Insects have 6, so spiders aren't insects. They're arachnids.
Insects have 6 legs!
Cats have a super bendy back, so they can twist around in the air and land on their feet!
Most dogs live about 10 to 13 years. Smaller dogs often live longer than big ones!
Most cats live about 12 to 18 years!
Sleep helps your body grow and rest, and it helps your brain remember what you learned!
Nobody knows for sure! Scientists think dreams might help your brain sort out what happened during the day.
Nobody knows for sure! Scientists think yawning might help cool down your brain or wake you up a little.
Sneezes blow tickly stuff out of your nose, and hiccups happen when the muscle under your lungs jumps suddenly!
Food gives your body energy to move, think, and grow!

answers.pattern: \bwhy do (we|people|i) (need to )?drink water\b|\bwhy is water important\b
answers.answer: Your body is more than half water! Drinking water helps you stay cool and keeps everything inside you working.

answers.pattern: \bwhy (is|are) vegetables\b|\bwhy do i have to eat (my )?vegetables\b
answers.answer: Vegetables are full of vitamins that help your body grow strong and fight off germs!
Germs are tiny living things too small to see. Washing your hands with soap gets rid of them so you don't get sick!
Grown-ups have 206 bones! Babies are born with around 300, and some of them join together as they grow.
Kids have 20 baby teeth, and grown-ups have 32 grown-up teeth!
Baby teeth fall out to make room for your bigger grown-up teeth, which are already growing underneath!

answers.pattern: \bwhat does (the|your|my) heart do\b|\bwhy does (the|my) heart beat\b
answers.answer: Your heart is a muscle that pumps blood all around your body, bringing it the oxygen it needs!
Blood is red because of something called hemoglobin, which carries oxygen and has iron in it!
Goosebumps happen when tiny muscles pull your hairs up, usually when you're cold or excited!
Before you were born, a cord connected you to your mom so you could get food. Your belly button is where it was!
Your brain is like your body's boss! It has billions of tiny cells that send messages to help you think, feel, and move.

answers.pattern: \bwhy do (we|people|i) get older\b|\bwhy do people age\b
answers.answer: As time goes by, our bodies slowly change. That's why kids grow up and grown-ups get gray hair!
Thomas Edison made the first light bulb that worked well enough for homes, back in 1879, though other inventors worked on it too!
Alexander Graham Bell got the first patent for the telephone in 1876!
The Wright brothers made the first powered airplane flight in 1903. It lasted just 12 seconds!
Lots of people helped build the internet! Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn are often called the fathers of the internet.

answers.pattern: \bwho was the first (person|man|human) on the moon\b|\bfirst\b.*\bon the moon\b
answers.answer: Neil Armstrong was the first person to walk on the Moon, in 1969!
George Washington was the first president of the United States!
There isn't one! Numbers go on forever. You can always add 1 to make a bigger number.
Infinity is the idea of something that never ends, like counting forever!
Airplane wings are shaped so that air pushes them up as the plane zooms forward!
Boats push water out of the way, and the water pushes back up on them! That's why they float.
Electricity is energy from tiny moving particles. It powers lights, TVs, and computers like the one I live in!
Magnets have an invisible pull that sticks to some metals, like iron. They have two ends called poles!
When water freezes, it spreads out a little, so ice is lighter than the same amount of water and floats!
An echo is your sound bouncing off something like a wall or a cliff and coming back to your ears!

answers.pattern: \bhow does a rainbow\b|\bwhat colou?rs are in a rainbow\b
answers.answer: A rainbow has red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet!

answers.pattern: \bhow are (babies|baby animals) made\b|\bwhere do babies come from\b
answers.answer: That's a great question to ask your mom, dad, or another grown-up you trust!
They're not real, but they're so much fun in stories and games! Some real animals are amazing too, like Komodo dragons, which are giant lizards.
Christmas is on December 25th every year!
Halloween is on October 31st every year!
New Year's Day is January 1st!
I don't have a clock, but your device or a grown-up can tell you the time!
I don't have a calendar, but a grown-up or your device can tell you what day it is!
Bananas are yellow when they're ripe! They start out green.
Grass and leaves are green, because of something inside them called chlorophyll that helps them make food from sunlight!
The Sun is actually white, but it looks yellow or orange from Earth because of the air!

answers.pattern: \bis (santa|santa claus|the easter bunny|the tooth fairy)( really)? real\b
answers.answer: That's a great question to talk about with your family! What do you think?
Nobody knows who made the very first candy! Long ago, people made sweets with honey, and later with sugar.

answers.pattern: \bwhy (can't|cant|can not|do) i (have to )?(stay up( late)?|go to bed|go to sleep)\b|\bhow come i (have to|gotta|must) go to (bed|sleep)\b|\bwhy do (i|kids) need (to )?sleep\b
answers.answer: Sleep helps your body grow and gets your brain ready for a new day! That's why grown-ups set bedtimes.
